notes:
I couldn't write the Proverbs 18 notes. My research tools stopped working before I could read any of the sources, so I have nothing from those pages to report.

I sent requests for five pages at once:
- the Enduring Word chapter commentary: https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/proverbs-18/
- the Precept Austin commentary: https://www.preceptaustin.org/proverbs-18-commentary
- the NET Bible notes: https://netbible.org/bible/Proverbs+18
- the Bible Hub commentary pages for v. 21 and v. 24

The pages came back, but my script crashed before showing any of their text. When I tried to fix it, I was told I had no tool uses left for this turn.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, give a URL for every point, and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. Since I read nothing, any verse notes I wrote now would have to come from memory, so I've left them all out.

**Next step:** say "continue" in a new message and I'll start again. I'll go through the chapter in this order:

1. **Traditional reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word, Precept Austin, and Gill, Ellicott and the Pulpit Commentary on Bible Hub or StudyLight.
2. **Differences between Protestant traditions:** this chapter probably has few. Where they exist, I'd look at:
   - v. 10, the name of the Lord: Spurgeon, Desiring God, Ligonier
   - v. 22, finding a wife and "favor from the LORD"
   - v. 24, the friend who stays closer than a brother, often read as pointing to Christ
3. **Other views:**
   - NET Bible notes on the hard Hebrew in vv. 1, 8, 19 and 24
   - Catholic and Orthodox readings, where New Advent or OCA comment on the chapter
   - GotQuestions and similar pages on how word of faith teaching uses v. 21 ("life and death are in the power of the tongue")
   - pages on whether v. 16 ("a man's gift") means a bribe, a present, or a spiritual gift

I'm sorry this round produced nothing you can use.
